newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico fears yr-end corn sales problems - Comagro.
newsitem.headline: Mexico fears yr-end corn sales problems - Comagro.

text.p: Corn traders in the western state of Jalisco foresee difficulties selling grain in December because of the possibility of a surge in imports, the manager of Comercializadora Agropecuario de Occidente (Comagro) said Tuesday.

"There will be problems for two reasons," he said. "One, if the government decides to open borders (to imports) but, two, the most difficult problem will be price," Rodlofo Lopez Macias said here in Comagro's home city. Comagro is one of Mexico's most prominent grains houses.
Jalisco, where Guadalajara is the capital, is the top corn producer state in Mexico with 100,000 growers. Estimated output for the June-December cycle this year is 2.2 million tonnes for the state.
Lopez Macias explained a downward trend in prices might cause social upheavals and an increase in the number of farmers owning past-due loans.
He said average production costs in the state are 3,500 pesos. He added that with an average yield per hectare of 3.2 tonnes the break-even price should be around 1,090 pesos per tonne.

Jalisco's current reference price is 1,250 pesos which could hold to December. "For six months' work, the grower is going to earn 2,090 pesos," he said. His calculation comes from the fact that Jalisco corn farmers have an average of almost six hectares each.
